newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin vows to end wage delays, misuse of funds.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin vows to end wage delays, misuse of funds.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday vowed to solve the problem of wage and pensions delays, which affect the living standards of millions of Russians, and to stop widespread misuse of state funds.
Yeltsin, who returned to work on Monday after bypass heart surgery, said in a radio address that wage delays were the most painful problem for his administration.
"The state's debt to the people is too high and the living standards are intolerably low," Yeltsin said in his usual stern and confident manner.
"I see my main duty in changing the situation," he added. "I will use all powers which you gave to me by electing me the Russian president for this."

Yeltsin said a series of planned steps aimed at stopping massive tax evasion and imposing stronger state control over the sale of alchoholic drinks could provide funds to help solve the problem of wage delays.
Wage delays which amount to trillions of roubles (billions of dollars) have triggered labour protests including a nationwide strike of coal miners.
Top military officials have warned that morale in the armed forces had sunk to a dangerously low point as most officers had not been paid since the summer.
Yeltsin said civil servants who misuse state funds were also to blame for the wage delays crisis.
"It's time to take measures against those who like living luxuriously at the state expense, or to be more exact at the expense of ordinary people," Yeltsin said.
He said he expected from the Prosecutor General and the Control Department of the presidential administration a detailed account of the steps they had taken to stop the misuse of budget funds.
"Officials in charge will have to answer for wrongdoings," Yeltsin said. "If one is stealing he should go to jail, If one is incompetent he should resign.
